en: Liturgical Text for the Memorial Service of the Great Master Zhiyi of Tiantai The assembly of monks performs three prostrations;
each person kneels alternately while burning incense and scattering flowers. The leader chants:
"I bow my head to the Teacher of the Tiantai School, Chan Master Fulong. Your divine discernment of Prajñā is boundless."
The light of liberation approaches;
let not its sound cease, for it resonates like an echo in a hollow valley.
Why doubt that this striking of the mechanism invokes true compassion?
They should come without fail.
I humbly consider that True Suchness is pure and serene.
Originally, there was no beginning to form or appearance;
the Dharma-realm encompasses all,
yet thus manifests the semblance of coming and going.
He manifests forms throughout the myriad phenomena and blends his traces within the various realms;
who knows that he has realized the sublime state of high attainment?
I can only look up to the depth of his pond and the greatness of his blossoms;
he possessed the extraordinary marks of the two sovereigns Yao and Shun,
and served as the honored teacher of the two kingdoms of Chen and Sui.
The teaching of the Dharma is perfectly harmonious,
and the subduing of demons is sovereign;
such is the majesty of his wisdom and meditative concentration.
The pervasive mists of compassion are immeasurable.
As the Sūtra says:
"Donning the robe of the Tathāgata."
He enters the Tathāgata’s chamber;
when sitting, he sits where the Tathāgata sits;
when walking, he walks where the Tathāgata walks.
They should be rubbed by the hands of the Tathāgata,
carried upon the shoulders of the Tathāgata,
and should be honored with the offerings due to the Tathāgata.
To make offerings to them brings merit that cannot be measured;
even a brief praise of it is difficult to exhaust.
Now, as we humbly encounter this occasion of commemorating the distant past at He-lin,
I venture to say that the fragrance of the sacrificial millet and grain is not what matters;
I merely offer this as an expression of my sincere devotion.
Looking up with reverent thought for your clear discernment:
at the initial time, once the proclamation has been made, one should immediately request [the precepts]. At other times, however, one simply omits the request;
having directly recited these words, [the procedure is complete].
He then expressed his intention with prostrations and praise, single-mindedly entreating the Great Master Zhizhe, the founder of the Tiantai school, saying:
"I only pray that you will descend to this ritual site and accept my offerings. He made these three requests, and all subsequent passages were modeled upon this.
With single-minded devotion, I invoke the High Patriarch of Tiantai, the Venerable Master Vasubandhu, and the Honored One Nāgārjuna.
With single-minded devotion, I invoke the Second Patriarch of the Tiantai school and its teachings, the Honored One of the Northern Qi.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Venerable Master Nanyue, the third patriarch and rightful successor of Tiantai.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Venerable Master Zhang’an, the fifth patriarch who compiled the treasury of the teachings of Tiantai.
With single-minded devotion, I entreat the Sixth Patriarch of the Tiantai Teaching and Contemplation, the Venerable Master of the Lotus Sūtra.
With single-minded devotion, I entreat the Seventh Patriarch of the Tiantai Teaching and Contemplation, the Venerable Master Tiangong.
With single-minded devotion, I entreat the Venerable Zuoxi, the Eighth Patriarch of the Tiantai teachings and contemplation.
With single-minded devotion, I entreat the Venerable Jingxi, the Ninth Patriarch and commentator on the Tiantai tradition.
Having finished the praise, he proclaimed the commentary, saying:
"The dharma-realm is perfectly interfused; the elephant has no form to be represented.
True Suchness is pure; the transformation has no being to be transformed."
Although the elephant has nothing it manifests,
there is nothing that it does not manifest;
its transformation has nothing it transforms.
There is nothing that is not transformed;
brilliantly manifesting the signs of two kings,
majestically serving as the teachers of two nations.
This concludes the words of gratitude for the conditions provided by Nanyue.
His reputation for the Way outweighs the value of Donglin; an earlier edition further states:
"The merit of his contribution to the Dharma is difficult to extol."
Now, as we happen to encounter the anniversary of the distant memorial,
we have briefly performed the rites of offering sacrifices;
the accompanying words of the memorial are set forth below.
Looking up, he addressed the assembly with these words:
"With single-minded devotion, I prostrate before the Great Master Tiantai Zhizhe, who practiced the Lotus Samādhi within Mount Dasu.
After the assembly below Tiantai Zhizhe had finished their prostrations and risen together, they offered praise."
The mind roams the Dharma-realm and all thoughts are stilled; Like the sun resting in space, yet not dwelling in space, The true mark of the three thousand worlds is suddenly and fully revealed.
The eighty thousand afflictions are equal to true purity;
The wondrous assembly on Vulture Peak is seen with longing clarity, And the entire body within the jeweled stupa is perceived with perfect distinctness.
Were it not for having personally encountered the Master of Nanyue, who among people would recognize such profound marks of dhyāna?
Therefore, with single-minded devotion, I take refuge and prostrate; let one bow descend according to this principle.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Venerable Zhiyi of Tiantai, who, while subduing the hosts of heavenly Māras atop Mount Huading, sat alone in meditation upon a fragment of stone;
his mind was all the more pure as the cold embraced deep clouds and the night was far from ended.
Suddenly, a thousand peals of thunder shook the earth as they came, and a hundred hidden monsters surged toward the heavens.
At the beginning of his awakening, ghosts and spirits were just dispersing and vanishing; he returned to his parents with renewed intimacy.
Through the power of the harmonious integration of the firm and the supple, and the stillness of illumination, a divine monk appeared and personally offered praise.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate before the Vaguan Monastery, where the subtle meaning of the Lotus Sūtra was revealed by the Dharma-body, the Tiantai Master Zhiyi.
The Gṛdhrakūṭa Peak proclaims this sutra as wondrous; for over forty years, it was kept secret and not spoken.
This family legacy must be transmitted to a legitimate heir; the crest-jewel is not obtained by following mere merit.

Both the provisional and the ultimate are majestically realized only by the Buddha; the vastness of the fundamental and the manifested is such that even those in the position of succession remain in doubt.
The Wise One personally heard it at that time; now at Waguan Temple, he explains it once more with clarity.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate before the Wise One of Tiantai, who, while preaching the *Mohe Zhiguan* in the precious pavilion of Yquan, was then his very self.
For ninety days, the compassionate rain opens the practice of the Perfect Way; The ten dharmas are discussed in harmony to establish the wondrous vehicle.
The precious chariot is lofty, vast, and fully adorned; The white ox is fat and strong, treading a level and upright path.
Tranquil and secure, it traverses the four conditions upon the direct road, Able to pass through the ten realms and reach the cool pond.
The world is filled with those riding broken donkey-carts;

I bow my head to the Tiantai Master, who vowed to be our refuge, and with single-minded devotion I pay homage to the Great Sage Zhiyi of Tiantai when he was lecturing on the *Benevolent Kings Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* atop the Taiji Hall.
A hundred seats surround like stars encircling the North Pole; The Four Reliances rise like the moon from the eastern sea.
The Eightfold Eloquence flows forth as the myriad nations find peace; The Twofold Emptiness expands as the thousand calamities disperse.
Fingers of jade compete to strike, their resonance echoing through the golden hall; Incense of ox-head burns thickly, its fragrance ascending from the beast-shaped censers.
I bow my head to the towering one whose body embodies the five patiences, who is worthy of receiving the reverent prostrations of ten thousand chariots—
the Great Master Tiantai Zhiyi, who at the time of bestowing the Sudden Precepts upon the two imperial consorts of the Chen and Sui dynasties manifested his true body.
The jade pendants chime resonantly as they encircle the Dharma-seat; The golden incense burners drift with fragrant smoke before the Teacher of Men.
With hands joined in prostration, all seek to don the sash of the precepts; With unblinking eyes, they gaze upon the compassionate countenance.
The five virtues are brilliant and pure like the full moon; The two adornments are profound and vast like the ocean depths.
A lion among men, a dragon within the Dharma; from this time forth, the Sovereign of Sui honored him as Zhizhe.

With single-minded devotion, he prostrated himself before the Buddha at Fulong and the Bodhi tree. Having realized the Pure Name Samādhi, when he lectured, his body was that of the Tiantai Master Zhizhe.
Walking the path, the frosty forest and fragrant trails are pure; With a tranquil mind, the moonlit trees and stone chambers are cold.
The clarity and purity of one's practice are known only to oneself; To what mortal can these profound and secluded realms be revealed?
Taking up the brush, I may have done so by the command of the Sui Emperor; Yet when the sutra was opened, a foreign monk appeared in response.

At that time, we regretted not having met him; we take refuge in the Sea of Chan-Wisdom of Tiantai and prostrate with single-minded devotion to the Venerable Zhiyi of Tiantai, who opened the ten thousand passages on the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra* upon the shores of Ling-shi.
A single point of autumn light upon the sea and mountains, amidst golden pavilions and towering layers of emerald barriers;
ten thousand phrases unfold the gates of liberation, while thousands of disciples vied to enter the chamber of compassion.
By nightfall, the sutra desk reflects the moon over the river hamlet, and the lecture bell’s cold resonance pierces through the water-side village homes.
The Three Virtues further nourish the clarity of the Three Contemplations; there is no one who has not partaken to their heart’s content of the flavor of the *amṛta*.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Master Zhizhe of Tiantai, who lectured upon the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa Sūtra* by the放生池 (Fangsheng Pool) and whose physical body was like flowing water.
The ark floats upon the clear river; The Dharma words resound within the heart of the azure waves.
Fragrance drifts from both banks as village elders follow; From midstream, the sounding of the *ghaṇṭā* causes golden scales to leap.
In the prison, Ji Xu once faced peril; Within the Meditation Hall, he resolved to repay his debt of gratitude.
Now, as before, the stone beams are many; with eyes of compassion, look upon us from other realms.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the golden spire of Shicheng, where the tranquil body of the Great Calming and Insight (Śānti) of the Twin Trees—Tiantai Zhizhe—is manifest.
The fire of transformative conditions has been extinguished and the mechanism of the fuel exhausted;
sitting upright in profound stillness before the stone image, his sons wail and cry, yet he does not return. For the masses of sentient beings, blinded and ignorant, who shall provide guidance?
The stars and riverbanks are dim, the golden ripples have faded, and amidst the whistling winds of the cloud-valleys, the cranes’ trees droop low.
The hundred pieces of gold and the wondrous medicine were entrusted to Zhang’an; yet I still regret that there was no one to transmit his Chan wisdom.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate before the tree at Fulong Mountain and the imperial memorial pagoda containing the entire body of the Tiantai Master Zhiyi.
Seated in the full lotus posture, he resembles one in tranquil meditation; The closed stupa is like a sealed chamber of meditative concentration.
In the early night, drifting light penetrates the distant forest; At times, a snap of the fingers is heard within the deep courtyard.
Year after year, the purple edict departs from the Golden Gate; Age after age, the imperial splendor opens the Stone Gate.
Finally, upon opening the seal, the old body was lost; one knows not to which direction it has gone.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Master Zhizhe of Tiantai, whose bodies manifest throughout the Buddha-lands of the ten directions.
With a compassionate heart, may your divine eye behold from afar;
Having already sown the seeds of past affinities in more than sixty states upon fertile fields, You must now provide the sweet rain for their sprouting shoots.
The father departs, leaving behind only medicine for after his passing; Separated from kin, one holds fast to a pearl within a drunken stupor.
I vow to revisit the Buddha-ridges of this land of China; may all sentient beings swiftly be led to open the Buddha-wisdom.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the High Patriarch of Tiantai, the Fearless Master, and the Venerable Nāgārjuna.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Venerable Master of the Northern Qi, the Second Patriarch of the Tiantai Teaching.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Venerable Master of Nanyue, the Third Patriarch and rightful successor of Tiantai.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Fifth Patriarch, Venerable Zhanran of Zhang’an, who compiled the treasury of the Tiantai teachings.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Sixth Patriarch, Venerable Fahua, who perfected the Tiantai teachings and contemplation.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Seventh Patriarch of the Tiantai Teaching and Contemplation, Venerable Tiangong.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Eighth Patriarch of the Tiantai Teaching and Contemplation, Venerable Zuoxi.
With single-minded devotion, prostrate to the Ninth Patriarch, the Venerable Jingxi, Master of the Tiantai Commentaries.
Having prostrated, each kneels, burns incense, scatters flowers, and silently cultivates the ten minds in both their direct and reverse orders.
Having cultivated these ten minds,
one should visualize oneself before all the Three Jewels and the various patriarchs,
and perform the rite of repentance.
With a sincere heart, I repent:
myself and all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm of the ten directions,
from the beginningless time of ignorance until now.
Following consciousness, the outflows, fetters,
and latent tendencies move the body, speech, and mind,
conforming to greed, hatred, and delusion.
They have committed the transgressions of the seven heinous crimes and the five rebellious acts;
they have violated the ten grave precepts and the four pārājika offenses;
and they have slandered the true teachings of the Three Vehicles.
The five kinds of Dharma masters of Pingling practice the four perversions and five perversions; while seated, they lack shame and remorse,
regarding the three miserable realms as if they were pleasure gardens.
They take the eight sufferings as their adornment;
in birth after birth they are born into families of wrong views,
and life after life they emerge in empty worlds where no Buddha dwells.
For what reason have I today, by chance, obtained a human body,
followed the example of those who renounce the world on the Snowy Mountains,
and encountered the bequeathed teachings of Tiantai?
I only regret that dark clouds have long obscured [the truth] and the net of views has become entangled;
thus, the thousandfold provisional and real dharma-gates remain unmanifest.
He recklessly claims to have "touched the fish" regarding the subtle contemplation of the Ten Dharmas that Complete the Vehicle,
yet this has never once entered his mind;
he is like one standing by a pond who merely envies the fish therein.
Failing to understand how to return home to weave their nets,
these foolish monkeys have not yet been caged;
they continue to fly far and wide within the forest of the five sensory objects.
Like thirsty deer facing the sun,
they gallop forever through the marshes of the six realms of desire; thus,
they cause their own bodies to surround the Dharma seat.
The mind wanders amidst the conditions of sensory dust;
the followers of the Eightfold Melody thunder like peals of lightning,
while the arrogance of the Fourfold Eloquence presents itself as a mere milky hue.
Furthermore, you deride the sacred scriptures and treat the instructional texts with contempt;
how can you possibly contemplate the entire body of the Dharma-Buddha?
How could one have imagined that for the sake of a half-verse from the Snowy Mountains,
one would now incur the retribution of being summoned by ignorance and darkness,
and visited by the consequences of perverse delusion?
The transgression of slandering others and being arrogant toward the Dharma creates obstacles for ten thousand kalpas and thousands of mountains;
such evils are immeasurable and boundless.
I lay bare my faults before the Triple Gem and confess them toward the Four Reliances,
severing the continuity of these thoughts.
Abandoning the mind of concealment,
may all universally receive the light of repentance.
Having performed the pure repentance for all transgressions, which are as vast as space, I single-mindedly take refuge and prostrate universally.
With a sincere heart, I entreat you:

in a single thought-moment and at one time, may you all entreat the Tathāgatas throughout the ocean of lands in the ten directions to universally turn the wheel of Dharma for the sake of sentient beings, and not pass into parinirvāṇa or return to quiescence.
To the noble and holy ones of the three vehicles, all those who dwell in the world with compassion,
acting solely as conditions for the benefit and happiness of sentient beings— I exhort you all and prostrate with body and mind;
having made this exhortation, I take refuge with a single-minded devotion.
I rejoice with a sincere heart.
From the first generation of the mind of enlightenment, through oceans of kalpas of practice,
until the attainment of Bodhi and even unto Nirvāṇa and the distribution of relics— may all Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within the void of the Dharma-realm [be honored].
The karma of non-arising of the noble ones of the Three Vehicles, the tainted causes of ordinary beings who practice the ten virtues,
and even the smallest roots of goodness such as a single prostration— I bear them all upon my head with joy;
having rejoiced in them with a single-minded devotion, I take refuge and pay universal homage.
With a sincere heart, one dedicates [the merit]:
from the beginning up to the point of sympathetic joy,
may all roots of goodness cultivated through the three karmas be dedicated into the ultimate reality of empty space, so as to equally bring benefit and happiness to the realm of all sentient beings.
May all the merit and wisdom cultivated be brought into harmony; may the bodies and lands thus accomplished be entirely adorned.
At the final moment, amidst a multitude of atoms at the site of enlightenment, may they universally attain perfect awakening together with all sentient beings.
Having performed this dedication, I single-mindedly take refuge and prostrate to all.
With a sincere heart, I make this vow:
May I always follow and learn from all Buddhas, practicing through oceans of lands as numerous as motes of dust for kalpas;
may I grind my bones to write out the sutras until they equal Mount Sumeru, and sacrifice my body for the sake of the Dharma throughout the entire realm of saṃsāra.
Proclaiming the perfect and eternal teachings of all Buddhas, Revealing the gate of liberation for all sentient beings,
Although having already attained ultimate Buddha-enlightenment, One does not abandon the practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
The original vow-text is recorded here:
May I, throughout all my lives, have no other thoughts, But follow exclusively the wondrous teachings of Tiantai.
When sounds and fragrances roar and surge, let my emotions cease their wavering; When fame and profit flow like a vast pool, let them not steal my resolve.
Unfurling scrolls to examine the subtle mysteries beneath the night clouds of the mountain hermitage, I fix my mind to seek out the hidden depths within the snow-chambered room.
The various patriarchs have transmitted the ocean-deep sea of great vows; may they always provide secret assistance so that [all beings] may attain awakening.
Having made this vow, with a single mind take refuge and prostrate universally.
*Text for Ritual Recitation and Praise on the Anniversary of the Memorial of the Great Master Zhizhe of Tiantai*
